Collin Corbett

Independent candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Illinois · Challenger

Political strategist (former Republican strategist); small business owner

Collin Corbett is a political strategist from Palatine who worked for Republicans before leaving the party, and he is running for Illinois governor as an independent. He filed his nominating petitions with the Illinois State Board of Elections on May 26, 2026, with former McHenry County Board member Carolyn Schofield as his running mate for lieutenant governor. An objection to his petitions, filed by Republican lieutenant governor nominee Aaron Del Mar, was withdrawn in June 2026, so Corbett stays on the November 3 ballot.

Where Corbett stands

Political approach
Calls himself a fiscal conservative and social moderate. Says the two parties have become polarized and that Illinois voters are ready for a choice outside them.
Economy
Argues that since JB Pritzker took office, Illinois ranks 46th among states in GDP growth, 45th in job growth and 39th in income growth.
Taxes and school funding
Supports cutting taxes and changing how local schools are funded. Says he wants to lower property taxes and the cost of living.
Housing
Says he wants housing to be affordable and good quality while keeping the value of existing homes stable.

Background

  • Political strategist who worked for Republicans for about 20 years, then left the Republican Party
  • Small business owner; lives in Palatine, Illinois
  • Filed nominating petitions as an independent candidate for governor on May 26, 2026, reported as about 37,000 signatures
  • Reported to have put $500,000 of his own money into the campaign
